item.title: Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.31851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the corrected Bessis--Moussa--Villani pinching conjecture for all symmetrized word averages. For Hermitian matrices $A,B$ and $D=E_A(B)$, we construct a positive compactly supported measure $\zeta_{A,B}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ such that \[ \Tr f(xA+yB)-\Tr f(xA+yD) =y^2\int_{\mathbb R^2}f''(xa+yb)\,d\zeta_{A,B}(a,b). \] Its total mass is $\frac12\|B-D\|_2^2$. This representation proves the corrected conjecture, including its equality cases, and gives a positive bivariate moment representation for the coefficient differences. We also derive complete monotonicity of normalized exponential pinching defects and a comparison with Lie--Trotter approximations. A one-dimensional second-order loss measure is obtained for trace-preserving conditional expectations on finite tracial von Neumann algebras. Finally, we relate $\zeta_{A,B}$ to Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure by an explicit positive radial transform.
item.dc:creator: Trung Hoa Dinh, Cong Trinh Le, Trung Dung Vuong

item.title: Perturbed Exponential Systems, Pattern-Dependent Shifted-Sinc Operators, and Matrix Symbols on Finite Unions of Intervals
item.description: arXiv:2610.31956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study perturbed exponential systems and unions of shifted frequency lattices through shifted-sinc operators and finite-dimensional fiberizations. For the auxiliary binary local-shift model, we identify the exact pattern-dependent invariant $$ \rho_{\delta,s}=\|P_-T_{2\delta}P_+\|, $$ which gives the optimal squared synthesis bounds $1\pm\rho_{\delta,s}$. For periodic patterns, the synthesis operator reduces exactly to a single constant Vandermonde-type matrix, yielding finite-dimensional basis criteria and optimal bounds. We further prove that the worst binary lower bound is the infimum of its periodic counterparts; at the critical value $\delta=1/4$, a step pattern is governed by a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has vanishing lower bound, although every fixed periodic pattern remains invertible. We also combine exact bounds for structured patterns with a support-independent perturbation estimate, obtaining explicit stability neighborhoods. For finite unions of bounded intervals and finitely many shifted lattices, folding modulo one yields finitely many rectangular phase matrices whose singular values and ranks give the exact bounds and complete Riesz-sequence, frame, and Riesz-basis criteria. This framework also yields finite Hadamard constraints for periodic spectra and an exact reduction of rationally commensurate multirate sampling.
item.dc:creator: Pierluigi Vellucci, Gohin Shaikh Samad

item.title: Block Toeplitz Operators, Matrix Valued Truncated Toeplitz operators, and Conjugations
item.description: arXiv:2610.32170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we characterize the complex symmetry of block Toeplitz operators on the Hardy-Hilbert space H2(E) with conjugation C_{u,\lambda}, where E is a finite dimensional Hilbert space. We also extend the application of this conjugation to matrix valued truncated Toeplitz operators.
item.dc:creator: Rewayat Khan

item.title: Nadler Theorem on Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a generalized metric space endowed with a weighted graph and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of fixed points for set-valued mappings that satisfy a contractive condition only along the links of the graph. To demonstrate the applicability and significance of our results, several illustrative examples are presented. As an application, we establish the solvability of a class of integral problems involving set-valued data.
item.dc:creator: Ismat Beg, Muhammad Aslam Javed

item.title: $L$-tauberian operators and subspaces with equi-integrable unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.32432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the class $LW_+$ of $L$-tauberian operators and its dual counterpart, the class $MW_-$ of $M$-cotauberian operators. We obtain sequential, perturbative, and algebraic characterizations of these classes. As a consequence, every $T\in LW_+(E,Y)$ is disjointly non-singular, and the converse implication holds if and only if every dispersed subspace of $E$ has equi-integrable unit ball. For $E=L_p$, the latter property depends on $p$. For $1\leq p<2$, equi-integrability of the unit ball is equivalent to dispersedness, and $L$-tauberian operators coincide with disjointly non-singular operators, while for $p\geq 2$ these equivalences fail. Moreover, $LW_+(L_p)$ is neither open nor stable under composition. Applying a result of Haydon, Odell, and Schlumprecht, we show that for $2<p<\infty$ every infinite dimensional dispersed subspace of $L_p$ contains an infinite dimensional subspace with equi-integrable unit ball. However, we give an example showing that this is not true for $p=2$.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Caldera, Manuel Gonz\'alez

item.title: Joint q-Numerical Ranges of Continuous Operator-Valued Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a unified theory of joint $q$-numerical ranges $\Fq(F)$ for continuous functions $F:\Om \to \B(\cH)$, where $\Om$ is a compact Hausdorff space and $\B(\cH)$ denotes the $C^*$-algebra of bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $\cH$. We prove that $\Fq(F)$ is totally bounded in $\cC(\Om)$, the space of continuous complex-valued functions on $\Om$, and establish the upper semicontinuity of the set-valued map $F\mapsto \Fq(F)$, and show that $\Fq(F)$ is compact when $\cH$ is finite-dimensional. The main result of the paper is a realization theorem. We prove that, for every totally bounded subset $K$ of $\cC(\Om)$ and every $q\in \C$ with $|q|=1$, there exist a Hilbert space $\cH$ and a continuous function $F:\Om\to\B(\cH)$ such that $qK\subset \Fq(F)\subset q\cok$. Consequently, if $K$ is closed and convex, then $\Fq(F)=qK$. As applications, we derive analogous realization results for bounded subsets in $\C^n$ and for totally bounded subsets in arbitrary Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: Amin Azadi

item.title: Restricted isometries in finite-dimensional $\ell^p$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $d,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ and $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$, we characterize all linear maps $s\colon\ell_d^p\to\ell_n^p$ for which there is $E\subseteq X_d$ such that $\|s(\xi)\|_p=\|\xi|_E\|_p$ for every $\xi\in\ell_d^p$. We call these maps \emph{restricted isometries}. Our Lamperti-type theorem gives a unique description of each such operator using a set transformation, a positive amplitude function, and a unimodular phase function. In particular, it includes noninjective and nonsurjective operators, even when the dimensions differ. We further characterize restricted isometries between finite $\ell^p$-spaces with arbitrary positive atomic weights. Applications include formulas counting set transformations and uniform restricted isometries, as well as a geometric description of all restricted isometries with fixed column supports.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Dalfollo-Daley, Alonso Delf\'in, Christina Fern\'andez, Cameron Mars, Xintan Xia

item.title: Effective Multiplicative Ergodic Theorems for Banach Space Cocycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.31921v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The multiplicative ergodic theorem (MET) describes the asymptotic growth rates of $q$-volumes under the iterates of an operator cocycle, i.e., compositions of operators driven by a stationary process, organizing the underlying space into equivariant filtrations or splittings into so called Oseledets subspaces. For operator cocycles in finite dimensions, and more generally in Hilbert spaces, one can control the geometry of the Oseledets subspaces given by the MET via the convergence rates of finite-time volume growth data. This makes the MET "effective" for matrix and Hilbert-space operator cocycles. We extend this effective theory to cocycles of Banach-space operators, obtaining quantitative angle estimates that are new even in the finite-dimensional setting. We take a sequential approach \`{a} la Raghunathan and Ruelle, allowing us to separate the geometric argument of the MET from measure-theoretic considerations. This permits weaker cocycle measurability hypotheses for the non-invertible and semi-invertible METs on a broad class of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As an application, we establish the MET for transfer operator cocycles on $\operatorname{BV}[0,1]$ associated with jointly measurable random Lasota-Yorke maps.
item.dc:creator: Adam Zaidan

item.title: Weighted and nonlocal Poisson equations on domains with capacity density conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32070v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global H\"{o}lder solvability of weighted Poisson equations and related fractional problems. On domains satisfying a capacity density condition, a nonnegative measure with bounded support depth admits a bounded globally H\"{o}lder continuous zero-boundary solution if and only if it satisfies an interior Morrey-type growth condition. Conversely, uniform boundary decay estimates for solutions with localized nonnegative sources characterize the capacity density condition. Analogous characterizations are established for the restricted and spectral fractional Laplacians. Our approach is based on weighted strong barriers and also yields two-weight Hardy inequalities, compact trace embeddings, and global H\"{o}lder solvability for nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators.
item.dc:creator: Takanobu Hara

item.title: Displacement structure and eigenvalue bounds for multiband prolate matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32082v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain explicit non-asymptotic bounds for the eigenvalue transition of multiband prolate matrices. Let $S\subset[-1/2,1/2]$ be a finite union of pairwise disjoint intervals, and let $\lambda_0\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_{N-1}$ be the eigenvalues of $B_{N,S}$. If $\nu$ is the number of boundary points of $S$ on the frequency torus, then, for every $0<\eps<1/2$, \[ \#\{k:\eps<\lambda_k<1-\eps\} \le \nu\ceil{\frac{\log(4N)}{\pi^2} \log\!\left(\frac{4}{\eps(1-\eps)}\right)}. \] Compared with the multiband estimate of Zhu and Wakin~\cite{wakin2017approximating}, this improves the dependence on $\eps$ from order $1/[\eps(1-\eps)]$ to logarithmic dependence. We also prove a second bound in which the main logarithmic term depends on the time--bandwidth product $N|S|$ rather than only on $N$. We also compare $S$ with frequency sets having fewer boundary points. Using a classical large-sieve estimate, we take into account not only the total size of the change in the frequency set, but also how that change is distributed. For sets with many small gaps, this can give a bound growing like $\log N$ for fixed $\eps$, even when the bounds based only on the total size of the gaps grow at least linearly in $N$. We also obtain exponential bounds for individual eigenvalues and use them to estimate the error in approximating sampled multiband signals by leading eigenvectors. A discretization argument gives corresponding results for the continuous problem. Numerical examples compare the bounds and examine how the locations of the frequency intervals affect the eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Luis Gomez, Hana Huber, Azita Mayeli

item.title: On the Propeller Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.32158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We simplify and improve OpenAI's proof of the propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor from 2008: the sum of the squared lengths of the Gaussian moments of any partition of Euclidean space is at most $9/(8\pi)$. We show equality only occurs for three 120 degree sectors in the plane (up to symmetries, measure zero changes, and taking orthogonal cross products with Euclidean space). We also remove computer assistance from the three-dimensional case of the conjecture, which previously used an epsilon net traversal.
item.dc:creator: Steven Heilman

item.title: Weak-$L^\infty$ and BMO with Hausdorff Content
item.description: arXiv:2610.32231v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ on measure space was introduced by Bennett et al. (Ann. of Math., 113(1981), 601-611) and proved to contain the space of $L^\infty$ and possess the appropriate interpolation property. In this paper, we are aimed to continue this line of research on the Euclidean space $\mathbb R^n$ endowed with Hausdorff content, which is a low-dimensional outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and fails to be additive or absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measures. But low-dimensional subsets, such as fractals, of $\mathbb{R}^n$ are Hausdorff capacitable. Precisely, in the setting of Hausdorff content, an analogue of weak-$L^\infty$ is defined and proved to possess an improved Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem. Moreover, we show that the space of functions with bounded mean oscillation associated to the Hausdorff content is embedded into this new weak-$L^\infty$ space by establishing a key estimate for the distribution via a packing condition. As a by-product, the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood operator on the space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ is established.
item.dc:creator: Hao Guo, Long Huang, Yangzhi Zhang, Ciqiang Zhuo

item.title: Hardy inequalities on the positive integer lattice: a dimensional transition
item.description: arXiv:2610.32858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine exactly in which dimensions the sharp Hardy coefficient on the positive integer lattice agrees with that on the positive Euclidean cone, with Dirichlet conditions on every coordinate face. Equality holds in dimensions one and two, whereas the discrete coefficient is strictly smaller in every dimension at least three. An exact transformation identifies the lattice problem with a weighted Dirichlet problem on a cube. A tangential integration identity evaluates the defect of an explicit critical profile and proves the dimensional transition. The continuous coefficient remains the lower edge of the essential spectrum of the transformed operator; below that edge, the sharp discrete coefficient is a simple eigenvalue with a positive eigenfunction. In dimension three, an explicit supersolution places the coefficient strictly between twelve and forty-nine quarters. A representation on a product of three-dimensional spheres relates the spectral threshold to the local geometry of the transformed problem.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Lizama

item.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollob\'as and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Guti\'errez, Bernu\'es, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollob\'as and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno

item.title: Variational principles and aplications to symmetric PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2403.18467v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we explore various equivalences of Ekeland's variational principle within the framework of group-invariant mappings. We introduce and analyze several key theorems, including the Drop theorem, the Petal theorem, Caristi-Kirk fxed-point theorem, and Takahashi's theorem, all of them within this context. Moreover, we extend the classical Drop theorem and Petal theorem to a more generalized setting. We also demonstrate the practical signifcance of these findings through numerous applications to diverse areas of mathematics. In particular, in the context of partial differential equations, we explore their implications on the solution of the Plateau problem, and in control theory. We also extend the classical Pontyargin maximum principle.
item.dc:creator: Javier Falco, Daniel Isert

item.title: Monotonicity properties of Hadamard weighted geometric means of bounded sets of positive kernel operators
item.description: arXiv:2408.04357v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove new monotonicity properties for joint and generalized spectral radius and their essential versions, operator norm, Hausdorff measure of non-compactness and numerical radius of products and sums of Hadamard weighted geometric means of positive kernel operators on appropriate Banach function spaces. Our results extend recent results on weighted geometric symmetrizations of bounded sets of such operators defined on $L^2$. To our knowledge, several proved properties in this generality are new even in the finite dimensional case and also in the case of singelton sets.
item.dc:creator: Katarina Bogdanovi\'c, Aljo\v{s}a Peperko

item.title: Recent perspectives on the Invariant Subspace Problem
item.description: arXiv:2507.21834v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We review recent work connected with the invariant subspace problem for operators, in particular new developments in the last 15 years. In particular, we include discussions of almost-invariant subspaces, universal operators, specific classes of operators and new results in the framework of Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: I. Chalendar, J. R. Partington

item.title: A solution to a conjecture on the norm of the Copson operator minus the Identity for monotone sequences
item.description: arXiv:2609.23035v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the operator distance between the Identity and the Copson operator on the cone of nonnegative, nonincreasing sequences within the Lebesgue sequence spaces $\ell^p(\mathbb{N})$. By proving the exact value of this distance, we confirm a conjecture originally formulated by A. Ben Said, S. Boza, and J. Soria in ``The norm of Hardy-type oscillation operators in the discrete and continuous settings'' (\emph{Analysis and Applications}, 2025).
item.dc:creator: Achraf Ben Said, Amiran Gogatishvili

item.title: Azumaya descent and \'etale-local cyclotomic comparison: a noncommutative filtration
item.description: arXiv:2610.02870v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bhatt-Morrow-Scholze motivic filtration on topological Hochschild homology ($THH$) is extended to Azumaya algebras over quasisyntomic rings. We prove the Azumaya descent theorem: $THH$ of such an algebra is equivalent, as an underlying spectrum, to $THH$ of its center, normalized on $\pi_0$ by the reduced trace instead of the unit map. This comparison $\Phi_A$ is not shown to be \'etale-locally cyclotomic. But what is cyclotomic \'etale-locally is a separate Morita trace, agreeing with $\Phi_A$ only on $\pi_0$. The resulting transported filtration is exactly the center BMS filtration, well defined up to the automorphism ambiguity of $\Phi_A$. It is insensitive to the Brauer class, reflected instead by $K$-theoretic and module-categorical pairings $THH$ does not see. We establish the analogous statement for derived Azumaya algebras over connective $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings, under a connectivity hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: H\^ong V\^an L\^e, Alexander Zuevsky

item.title: The $L^2$-Cartesian Numerical Radii of Hilbert Space Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.04844v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let $T=H+iK\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be the Cartesian decomposition of $T$, where $H=H^{*}$ and $K=K^{*}$. We introduce the $L^2$-Cartesian numerical radius and study its basic properties. We compare it with the classical numerical radius $\omega(T)$. In particular, we establish the sharp estimate $ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\omega(T)\le \wcart{2}(T)\le \omega(T), $ and establish lower and upper bounds in terms of the Cartesian parts $H,K$. We also give an equality characterization and explicit sharpness examples. As a consequence, we obtain $\frac{1}{4}\left\|T^{*}T+TT^{*}\right\|\le \wcart{2}(T)^2\le \omega(T)^2. $ More generally, we study the $L^p$-Cartesian numerical radius and prove the sharp comparison $ c_p\,\omega(T)\le \wcart{p}(T)\le \omega(T),\qquad 1\le p<\infty. $ Finally, we present a block-operator analogue of the classical refinement of the triangle inequality.
item.dc:creator: Wasim Audeh, Fuad Kittaneh, Hamid Reza Moradi, Satyajit Sahoo

item.title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.24568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras. For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules. Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $\theta_{A_0}=\id$, $\theta_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose M\"uger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion, and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.
item.dc:creator: A. Zuevsky

item.title: Expansivity of algebraic semigroup actions
item.description: arXiv:2512.07445v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a semigroup $S$ and a right $\mathbb{Z}[S]$-submodule $J\leq \mathbb{Z}[S]^n$, we study expansivity of the algebraic action of $S$ induced on the Pontryagin dual of $\mathbb{Z}[S]^n/J$. We completely determine the class of semigroups for which expansivity of this action is characterized by the triviality of $J^\perp$, in terms of the existence of a finite subset $K\subseteq S$ such that $S=KS$. This condition is satisfied in particular by every monoid, and more generally by every semigroup with a left unital convolution Banach algebra, in which case we are able to extend the characterization of expansivity in terms of an invertibility condition when $J$ is finitely generated. We also exhibit examples of non-unital semigroups satisfying the hypotheses of our results.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Donoso-Echenique

item.title: Hilbert transforms on graph products of finite von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.00194v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Hilbert transforms on graph products of finite von Neumann algebras, with particular interest in their boundedness on the associated noncommutative $L_p$-spaces for $1<p<\infty$. We establish a generalized Cotlar identity for Hilbert transforms, valid on operators whose lengths exceed a constant depending only on the underlying graph. We further prove that graph products of finite von Neumann algebras satisfying a Haagerup-type inequality admit $L_p$-bounded Hilbert transforms, therefore extending the corresponding result of Mei and Ricard for free products of finite von Neumann algebras. In addition, we obtain several equivalent characterizations of this Haagerup-type inequality. Our results apply, in particular, to graph products of finite groups, right-angled Hecke von Neumann algebras, and graph products of finite quantum groups. As an application, we provide a complete characterization of a compactness problem posed by Ozawa for graph products of finite groups and right-angled Hecke von Neumann algebras.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Qi Lu, Runlian Xia

item.title: Characterization of the boundedness of the segment multiplier on rearrangement-invariant spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.22277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.
item.dc:creator: Miguel F. Barea-Fern\'andez, Ron Kerman, Jan Lang, Javier Soria
